rawAnswer: {"findings":[{"kind":"defect","severity":"medium","title":"Location filter drops diagnostics that belong to the consuming project","detail":"In analyzer mode, every diagnostic now goes through ReportIfLocatedInCompilation. It drops any diagnostic whose location is not a source tree of the current compilation. That goes further than dropping problems that belong to metadata types. Take a user type whose member is a metadata generic like Wrapper<UserType>, where UserType is a source type without [MessagePackObject]. GetObjectInfo walks the substituted members and calls CollectCore(UserType, metadataMember). MsgPack003 (TypeMustBeMessagePackObject) is then built at callerSymbol.Locations[0], which is a metadata location, and the filter drops it. CollectCore has already added UserType to alreadyCollected, so the later CollectCore(UserType, userProperty) call at line 660 returns early and never reports at the user's property. Before this change, the diagnostic was reported at the metadata location, which analyzers are allowed to do. Now a real problem in the consuming project is hidden, and the type gets no formatter without any warning. This conflicts with N1 and N2 and with the new README text.","hunkIds":["h3","h6"],"citations":[{"file":"src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs","side":"new","startLine":1339,"endLine":1345,"quote":"Location location = callerSymbol is not null ? callerSymbol.Locations[0] : formattedType.Locations[0];"},{"file":"src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs","side":"new","startLine":1444,"endLine":1450,"quote":"if (diagnostic.Location.IsInSource && this.compilation.ContainsSyntaxTree(diagnostic.Location.SourceTree))"},{"file":"src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs","side":"new","startLine":239,"endLine":239,"quote":"this.reportDiagnostic = reportAnalyzerDiagnostic is null ? null : diagnostic => ReportIfLocatedInCompilation(reportAnalyzerDiagnostic, diagnostic);"}]},{"kind":"defect","severity":"low","title":"Problems in referenced types are silently ignored, contrary to new docs","detail":"The README and MsgPack004.md now say that diagnostics for members of referenced-assembly types are reported by the defining project. For a third-party package that does not, the consuming project still generates a formatter for the open generic definition (CollectCore(type.OriginalDefinition)). Unattributed public members are left out of that formatter, and all related diagnostics are now dropped, so nothing tells the user that data will not be serialized. This is the kind of silent failure N1 warns about.
